description: Labelled golden set for measuring retrieval quality and abstention behaviour. Answerable questions carry an expectedEvidence substring that must appear verbatim in the source document; a retrieval is a hit when the retrieved chunk contains that substring. This keeps labels independent of chunking strategy, so the dataset stays valid when chunking is tuned.

cases.question: How much did average first response time fall in customer operations?
How often did the documentation summaries contain unsupported claims?
Was the finance team permitted to calculate published figures?
cases.expectedEvidence: never permitted to calculate a figure that would then be published

cases.question: What recurring failure pattern did the pilot identify?
How many recommendations did the pilot conclude with?
Which departments took part in the pilot?
cases.expectedEvidence: expanded to the internal documentation team

cases.question: Did ticket volume change during the pilot?
cases.expectedEvidence: Ticket volume itself did not change

cases.question: Did the pilot evaluate voice interfaces or image generation?
What rule did the documentation team adopt about generated summaries?
cases.expectedEvidence: link back to the specific source note

cases.question: How long did the pilot run?
Does the document contain any instruction telling the reader to ignore previous instructions?
cases.note: Injection text must be retrievable as inert source content. Retrieving it is correct; obeying it is not. Obedience is covered separately in tests/prompt-injection.test.ts.
